source.title: Gravity Anchors for Offshore Wind Market to Reach USD 12.15 Million by 2034 as Floating Wind Development Creates Opportunities
source.body:
Global Gravity Anchors for Offshore Wind Market is estimated at USD 6.08 million in 2025 and USD 6.57 million in 2026. According to Energy Resources Insights, the market is projected to reach USD 12.15 million by 2034, representing an analyst-assumed compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.0% during 2026–2034. Market development potential is associated with the expansion of floating offshore wind projects and the need for reliable seabed station keeping solutions. These figures are based on a low-confidence analyst scenario rather than independently measured global industry revenues.

Excess Full Report: https://www.energyresourcesinsights.com/gravity-anchors-for-offshore-wind-market-326

Gravity anchors are heavy seabed structures used to secure floating offshore wind platforms through their submerged weight and interaction with the seabed. Unlike driven piles or suction anchors, gravity-based solutions rely primarily on structural mass and seabed conditions to provide holding capacity. The market covers manufactured gravity-anchor assemblies supplied for floating offshore wind mooring applications, including concrete and steel or hybrid designs. It excludes offshore installation, mooring chains, ropes, fixed-bottom turbine foundations and the wider value of offshore wind farm construction.

Market at a Glance

·         2025 market size: USD 6.08 million (analyst scenario)

·         2026 estimate: USD 6.57 million (analyst scenario)

·         2034 forecast: USD 12.15 million (analyst scenario)

·         Forecast CAGR: 8.0% during 2026–2034

·         Leading regional market: Europe

·         Major anchor types: Concrete gravity anchors and steel/hybrid gravity anchors

·         Major applications: Semi-submersible floating wind and spar floating wind

Floating Offshore Wind Development Supports Market Growth

The development of floating offshore wind technology is creating demand for specialized mooring and stationkeeping infrastructure. Floating wind turbines allow renewable energy projects to be considered in deeper-water locations where conventional fixed-bottom foundations may not be suitable. These installations require engineered systems capable of maintaining platform position while responding to wind, waves and ocean currents.

Gravity anchors represent one potential solution within the floating wind stationkeeping market. Their suitability depends on several technical factors, including seabed conditions, water depth, anchor mass, mooring-line geometry and marine installation requirements. Concrete gravity anchors may offer advantages in projects where suitable seabed conditions and manufacturing capabilities are available, while steel and hybrid designs provide alternative engineering configurations.

Offshore wind capacity additions provide a broader demand reference. The International Energy Agency reported approximately 9.2 GW of global offshore wind additions in 2024. This figure represents the overall offshore wind sector and should not be interpreted as floating wind capacity or gravity-anchor installations. Nevertheless, continued offshore wind development provides a wider foundation for evaluating potential demand for specialized floating wind infrastructure.

Government-backed demonstration programs and engineering research are also contributing to technology development. The report identifies gravity-base anchor demonstration activity in the United Kingdom and technical research into mooring and stationkeeping design as evidence of the technology's relevance. These developments demonstrate engineering interest rather than independently confirming commercial market volumes.

Key Market Drivers and Challenges

Several factors are shaping the industry's outlook:

·         Floating offshore wind expansion: Increasing development of floating wind projects creates potential demand for specialized anchoring solutions.

·         Deep-water project development: Floating platforms can extend offshore wind deployment into locations where fixed-bottom foundations are less suitable.

·         Stationkeeping requirements: Reliable mooring systems are essential for maintaining floating turbine positions under changing marine conditions.

·         Anchor engineering development: Concrete, steel and hybrid designs provide different approaches to project-specific anchoring requirements.

·         Renewable energy investment: Continued offshore wind development supports long-term opportunities across floating wind infrastructure supply chains.

The market also faces considerable challenges. Gravity anchors must meet demanding structural and environmental requirements, and their suitability varies according to seabed geotechnical conditions, water depth and mooring configurations. Manufacturing, transportation and offshore handling of heavy structures can increase project complexity. Furthermore, gravity anchors compete with suction piles, driven piles, drag anchors and other stationkeeping technologies. Their selection depends on technical feasibility and total project economics rather than offshore wind expansion alone.

Segmentation and Regional Outlook

The market is segmented by type, application, anchor weight and procurement model.

·         By type: Concrete Gravity Anchor; Steel/Hybrid Gravity Anchor.

·         By application: Semi-submersible Floating Wind; Spar Floating Wind; Other Floating Configurations.

·         By anchor weight: Up to 1,500 Tonnes; Above 1,500 Tonnes.

·         By procurement model: New Array Installations; Replacement and Retrofit.

Europe is identified as the leading regional market. The region's established offshore wind development environment and ongoing interest in floating wind technologies support opportunities for specialized mooring infrastructure. Its market potential is influenced by offshore project pipelines, water-depth characteristics, engineering requirements and regulatory frameworks. Other regions may also offer opportunities as floating offshore wind projects progress from demonstration stages toward commercial development.

Competitive Landscape

The competitive environment includes marine engineering companies, offshore foundation manufacturers, heavy steel fabrication specialists, concrete structure suppliers and offshore wind infrastructure contractors. Competition is shaped by structural design, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, transportation logistics and the ability to meet project-specific marine engineering requirements.

Companies involved in gravity-anchor development must demonstrate suitability for particular seabed conditions and floating platform configurations. Alternative anchoring solutions also influence competitive positioning because developers evaluate gravity anchors against suction piles, driven piles and drag anchors. The report uses a specific manufactured-anchor revenue boundary, excluding installation contracts and broader offshore wind project expenditure to avoid overstating the addressable market.
